flow.grossPlain: Mastercard reports revenue already net of the $6,369M of rebates and incentives it pays banks and merchants to win card business — so there is no separate cost-of-revenue line in its books. The costs were taken out before revenue was counted.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Salaries, technology and offices for the people who run the network — by far Mastercard's biggest cost.

opex.name: Advertising and marketing
opex.note: Brand campaigns, sponsorships and the 'Priceless' advertising.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, data centers, equipment and acquired technology.

opex.name: Provision for litigation
opex.note: Settlements with merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation — Mastercard flags this as a special item.

follow100Note: Mastercard keeps about $47 of every $100 it books — one of the fattest profit slices in this whole series. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Mastercard nets its $6,369M of rebates and incentives against revenue before reporting it; the gross assessments behind them ($12,118M) are key metrics in its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
oneTimers: A $74M litigation provision — settlements with merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation — is flagged by Mastercard as a special item. Excluding it and a $5M equity-investment loss, adjusted net income was $4,653M and adjusted EPS was $5.31.
Mastercard bought back 5.3 million shares for $3.0B in the quarter and paid $763M of dividends, with $4.9B of buyback capacity left.
otherDetail: Other income (expense) was −$121M: $88M of investment income and $46M of other income, outweighed by $250M of interest expense and a $5M loss on equity investments.
pngFooterNote: Revenue is reported net of $6,369M of rebates and incentives.

segments.name: Payment network
segments.note: The toll for running the card network — the fees banks pay per swipe, after the $6,369M of rebates Mastercard pays to win and keep card business. Gross assessments before those rebates were $12,118M: domestic $3,211M, cross-border $3,841M, transaction processing $4,781M.

segments.name: Value-added services and solutions
segments.note: Everything beyond the swipe: fraud screening, data analytics, consulting, identity and cybersecurity tools sold to banks and merchants — now 41% of net revenue and the fastest-growing part.

takeaways.text: Value-added services net revenue hit $4,058M — fraud tools, data and consulting now bring in 41 cents of every revenue dollar, and they grew nearly twice as fast as the payment network itself (+11%).
takeaways.title: The services side is the growth engine

takeaways.text: Mastercard billed $12,118M of network assessments but handed $6,369M straight back to banks and merchants as incentives — and rebates grew 18%, faster than gross fees (+14%). The toll road keeps more traffic, but the toll-keepers bargain harder every year.
takeaways.title: Banks keep more of every swipe

takeaways.text: Gross dollar volume rose 7% to $2,952B and purchase volume 9%, with switched transactions up 9%. Cross-border volume — the most profitable kind, from travel and cross-border e-commerce — grew 11% in local currency.
takeaways.title: The world keeps swiping

verdict: Mastercard's net revenue rose 14% to $9.8B as global card spending stayed strong and its fraud, data and consulting services grew 19% — the toll road on the world's spending keeps getting wider.
